requirements.requirement: Existing data under /srv/inventory is owned by inventorysvc.
requirements.summary: Final and post-restart observations show the directory, data subdirectory, and both existing files owned by inventorysvc, with inventory-readers as their group.

requirements.requirement: The existing data is readable by inventory-readers.
requirements.summary: A process running as nobody with inventory-readers as its sole group successfully read and checksummed both files before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Other users cannot access the inventory data.
requirements.summary: Directories have mode 2750 and files mode 0640, leaving no permissions for others. Direct tests also show an unrelated user cannot read config.json or traverse /srv/inventory, both before and after restart.
The same two files remain present, and their post-restart SHA-256 hashes exactly match the preparation baseline and pre-change hashes.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct metadata, access-behavior, and checksum evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, an acknowledged restart, a changed boot ID, a running post-restart system, and recovered identities, permissions, access behavior, and data. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The unrelated-user read command directly tested config.json rather than records.csv, although records.csv has the same owner, group, mode, and protected parent path.
Requirement content_preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: All managed-system mutations had clear roles: creating the missing identities, repairing ownership and modes, and performing the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary troubleshooting mutation was identified. The only hygiene defect is the retained /tmp/inventory-reboot.log created by the restart command; it was low-risk but not cleaned up. No failed services, new network exposure, or package damage appeared afterward.
